verdicts.note: Comparative study of MATERNAL-AGE LIMITS in ART regulation. Legal eligibility is P2's exposure and this maps it across countries — the instrument a cross-national P2 design would need.
Nigeria; tag SECONDARY under Wall 8.
Dissertation on correlates of advanced-age first birth.
Infertility risk by sexual identity and race. B.3's (infection-driven sterility).
Global variation in single-embryo-transfer uptake — A.12's policy lever, seen from the practice side.

'AGE SHOCK': misperceptions of age and fertility BEFORE AND AFTER IVF, in women who conceived after 40. A within-person belief change around treatment — the closest P6 has come to identifying the belief mechanism on people who actually used ART.
No abstract. Advocacy piece on coverage as a right.

**The target the batch-3 letter was contesting.** Estimates the contribution of NON-ART ovulation stimulation to US SINGLETON as well as multiple births. Singleton contribution is squarely arm 1's estimand, and OI is the treatment margin the ART registries do not capture — the Australian data put it at 1.9% of births against ART's 4.8%. Priority.
Coverage for MALE infertility care — a coverage margin usually excluded even in mandate states.
No abstract. Elective oocyte cryopreservation for age-related decline.
IVF and human evolution — selection consequences, not fertility levels.
Critical sociology of reproductive stratification.
Normative argument about male-infertility coverage standards.

Kazakhstan: GOVERNMENT SUPPORT against IVF clinical pregnancy rates, public vs private clinics. Access exposure, per-cycle outcome — Wall 1 by outcome, but the exposure is exactly P1's and non-Western.

European Economic Review: FREE IVF and women's human-capital investment — the Israeli shock again, third record from it in the frame. Outcome is schooling, not births; the first stage is what A.17 needs.
Infertility and preservation access among US medical trainees.
No abstract. Clinical guidance on elective preservation.

Health Economics 2024: OPTIMAL FISCAL DESIGN of ART policy with heterogeneous fecundity. Theory rather than an estimate, but it formalises the access margin arm 2 measures and will discipline the chapter's mechanism section.

Systematic review of infertile couples' intentions regarding parenthood and RETURN TO ART. Treatment discontinuation and re-entry is the behaviour that decides how many treated couples ever reach a birth.
Spain: fertility RECUPERATION after postponement, by education and partnership trajectory. The non-ART route to the same recovery A.17 attributes to treatment.

**A THREAT-TO-IDENTIFICATION RECORD AND A LOAD-BEARING ONE. 65% of US workers are covered by SELF-INSURED employers exempt from state mandates under ERISA.** Every arm-2 estimate that treats 'state mandate' as the treatment is measuring a policy that does not bind for two-thirds of the workforce, which attenuates the effect toward zero by construction. This belongs in risk of bias for the entire P1 cell.
Review of fertility and ageing.

**AER 2017: IVF-induced fertility variation as an INSTRUMENT for having children, to estimate career effects.** Exactly A.12's twin-IV problem in A.17's frame: the paper is about careers, but its FIRST STAGE is A.17's estimand — how much fertility IVF actually produces, estimated on administrative data with clean identification and reported as a nuisance. Route to full-text first-stage extraction, not screened out.
'The fertility myth' — Israeli students' beliefs about late pregnancy IN AN ERA OF ART. Names the ART-specific belief rather than age knowledge in general.
Ovarian reserve screening ethics.

Demography 2011: MEDICAID EXPANSIONS and fertility. Not ART-specific — health-insurance access generally — but the same identification family and a useful benchmark for how large an insurance-driven fertility response can plausibly be.
Australian public funding and the shift to single embryo transfer; outcome is twin/triplet rates and government savings.
Whether BIOLOGICAL FERTILITY predicts realized family size. This tests A.17's premise directly: if biology does not bind, treating it cannot help much.
Dyadic adjustment in infertile couples.
Kazakhstan, age-fertility understanding among IVF patients.
Dutch desired family size over the life course.
Valuing infertility treatment through quality of life.
Fertility in inflammatory bowel disease.
NEJM cumulative live-birth rates per couple across cycles. Wall 1's canonical shape — but note it is the per-couple success parameter every P4 simulation needs as an input.
No abstract. ESHRE European IVF Monitoring annual report, 2003 edition.
No abstract. Childless women's knowledge of fertility and assisted reproduction.
No abstract; title is a claim: delayed childbearing is RARELY A CONSCIOUS CHOICE. If true it weakens P6's induced-postponement mechanism, so it is on-cell in the direction against.
Danish students' fertility awareness.

Norway: socio-demographic composition of ART births over time. Composition matters for arm 1 — if ART births concentrate among women who would have had children anyway, the additional share is smaller than the raw share.
Sterility in English parish registers. PM-era, and A.17 has no PM arm.
No abstract. Late motherhood: intentions, trends, consequences.
Public funding of uterus transplantation — a distinct technology at negligible scale.
Danish female healthcare professionals' attitudes.
Oocyte ageing mechanisms.
Infection-related infertility hospitalisation by country of birth. B.3's.

'EVER GROWING DEMAND FOR IVF DESPITE STABLE BIOLOGICAL FERTILITY - A EUROPEAN PARADOX.' Argues ART uptake is not tracking a biological need. If right, arm 1's share is measuring demand for treatment rather than repair of a constraint, which changes what the share means.
One-year follow-up after fertility counselling — an intervention with a follow-up, closer to behaviour than most of this cell.
Realization of fertility intentions under postponement, transitional vs post-transitional populations.

J. Population Economics: ART and women's career choice. Same first-stage argument as the AER 2017 record — the career literature is using ART-induced fertility variation and reporting A.17's parameter incidentally.
Fertility knowledge among oocyte DONORS.
No abstract; title decisive. Mandates and ART care DISCONTINUATION — the dropout margin, which is where treated couples fail to convert into births.
Companion to the Austrian record in batch 4: late fertility INTENTIONS against realized late fertility.
Iranian pre-marriage counselling; fertility preferences.
No abstract. PERCEIVED THREAT OF INFERTILITY against intention to ANTICIPATE childbearing — P6's mechanism running in the protective direction, i.e. fear of infertility pulling births earlier.
No abstract. Live birth rates after autologous oocyte cryopreservation by maternal age at transfer — a per-cycle outcome inside the elective-preservation population.
Iranian survey of childbearing decisions.

**European Journal of Population 2026, and it names P6's problem in its own title: 'Perceptions of Medically Assisted Reproduction and Fertility Postponement: LIMITED EVIDENCE, CRITICAL QUESTIONS.'** An independent statement that the belief-to-behaviour link is unestablished. The chapter should cite this rather than assert the gap on its own authority.
French public-health framing of infertility.
Attitudes to ART coverage in the US military health system.

US Births: Final Data 2013 — the vital-statistics denominator every US share calculation divides by. A.12's probe found the same series at the head of its primary cell; identities get tabulated, not identified.
